title: The Majestic Monolith can become The Citadel
summary: DHH's follow-up: most web apps should start and stay a monolith; when one slice has divergent performance needs, extract a single Outpost rather than carving everything into services.

assertions.quote: the vast majority of web applications will continue to be served well by The Majestic Monolith for their entire lifespan
Maybe you’re dealing with very large teams that constantly have people tripping over each other
The Outposts are there to allow the Majestic Monolith to offload a particular slice of divergent behavior

verdicts.note: Targeted extraction is a standard migration pattern and matches Shopify's and others' reports, but 'most of the benefit' is not quantified.

assertions.quote: As more and more people come to realize that the chase for microservices ended in a blind alley, the pendulum is going to swing back.

verdicts.note: There are prominent consolidation stories (Amazon Prime Video, Segment) but no survey establishes a net trend.

A systematic search of academic and grey literature found only four documented cases of switching from microservices back to a monolith, and the authors conclude it is still too early to call it a trend; retreats happen, but the record does not show many.
